thread.title: Assessing Amazon’s (AMZN) Competitive Strategy With Doorbell Startup Ring

title: Assessing Amazon’s (AMZN) Competitive Strategy With Doorbell Startup Ring
text:
Assessing Amazon’s (AMZN) Competitive Strategy With Doorbell Startup Ring March 01, 2018, 09:23:18 AM EDT By Richard Saintvilus Amazon (Shutterstock photo) 
Shares of Amazon ( AMZN ) continue to hit new all-time highs, reaching $1,528.68 Wednesday, climbing fractionally and seemingly immune to the Dow’s 380-point tumble in the last hour of trading. 
Wednesday’s stock performance could be attributed to Amazon’s acquisition of video-doorbell startup Ring, which some analysts are already calling the company’s smartest deal yet . Although the terms of the deal has not been disclosed, multiple reports have pegged the buyout price at north of $1 billion. And that’s a hefty sum for Ring, which, under its former name DoorBot, appeared on CNBC's "Shark Tank” in 2013, leaving with no deal. 
Fast forward five years later, Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos has given the small six-year-old startup more than a "ringing" endorsement. But what does Amazon get for its billion-dollar-bet, which marked its second-largest acquisition to date, you ask? 
Obviously, aside from UPS ( UPS ) and FedEx ( FDX ), few companies visit the doors of America households more than Amazon. As such, Bezos is seemingly doubling down on initiatives that enhances the company’s existing Key platform, which combines a smart security camera and a smart lock that allows guests or package-delivery personnel access to conduct in-home deliveries. 
As part the larger objective, Amazon wants to minimize deliveries left on doorsteps, which are exposed to theft or so-called "porch thieves.” Ring, which makes smart doorbells that allow homeowners to see who is at their door when the doorbell is pressed, fits right in with what Amazon is attempting to do. 
"We'll be able to achieve even more by partnering with an inventive, customer-centric company like Amazon. We look forward to being a part of the Amazon team as we work toward our vision for safer neighborhoods," Ring said in a statement. An Amazon spokesperson also confirmed the deal, saying, according to CNBC, "Ring's home security products and services have delighted customers since day one. We're excited to work with this talented team." 
This deal comes less than two months after Amazon acquired Blink, a Ring competitor that allows people view a live feed from their smartphones of their front door. As the race for home deliveries heats up from the likes of Walmart ( WMT ) and Target ( TGT ), Amazon is acquiring assets to widen its lead. But the deal for Ring is more than just battling brick-and-mortar. 
Owing to the success of its Alexa smart speaker, Amazon is positioning itself in the race for the smart home, where it competes with Apple ( AAPL ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ). The latter spent $3.2 billion to acquire smart thermostat maker Nest. The return on that Nest investment hasn’t been material enough for Google to disclose sales related to that product category. 
Will Amazon garner better success? Only time will tell. But for now, the company is looking to maintain its fixture at our doorsteps. And it has pulled off yet another deal that will force its competitors to respond.
